findings.title: Negative-offset comment is wrong and the change clamps offsets for every paginator
findings.body: The new comment says negative offsets are allowed for bidirectional pagination, but `max(0, offset)` on the non-prev path clamps them to 0. This is a silent behavior change for every BasePaginator subclass (DateTimePaginator, Paginator, etc.), not just the new optimized path. A client-supplied negative offset on a next cursor now quietly returns the first page instead of erroring. The comment misdescribes the code and the change is not covered by any test.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator raises on user-controlled cursors
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django does not support negative indexing on querysets and raises, so the request fails with a 500. `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets from the query string, so any superuser or global-access member who sends `optimized_pagination=true` with a negative offset cursor triggers this. The inline comments claim the path is 'safe' and that 'permissions are checked at the queryset level', but neither is true: the path crashes and offsets are not a permission boundary.

findings.title: Hidden query parameter switches paginator and cursor semantics for admins
findings.body: `optimized_pagination=true` silently selects a different paginator (OptimizedCursorPaginator with negative-offset support) for superusers and global-access members only. This is an undocumented, client-selectable behavior fork on an API endpoint. Cursors produced by one paginator may not be valid for the other, and the 'advanced' path is the one that can 500 (see paginator.py negative slicing). The non-admin path gets different behavior from the same URL with no documented contract.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result wholesale
findings.body: The new class copies almost all of `BasePaginator.get_result` and `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor`, differing only in the negative-offset branch. Any future bug fix in BasePaginator (such as the `queryset.query.order_b` typo in build_queryset) must be made in two places, and the two will drift. The divergence that matters is only the negative-offset branch, which is the broken part.

findings.title: Segments are silently truncated to 1000 spans with no metric or log
findings.body: The script now `zpopmin`s the lowest-scored spans whenever a segment exceeds 1000 entries. Those spans are deleted from Redis with no metric or log, so data loss is invisible. Previously, `_load_segment_data` skipped oversized segments and logged `segment_span_count_exceeded`. That check was removed from Python in this PR, and `max_segment_spans` is now unused. The cap also silently drops spans that may include parts of the segment the user cares about, based only on end timestamp order.

findings.title: Redirect-chain walk limit reduced from 10000 to 1000 without justification
findings.body: The loop limit went from 10000 to 1000, and the explanatory comment about deep segment trees was removed. Traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 are now not joined correctly, with no metric or warning. This is an unrelated behavior change folded into a buffering-optimization PR.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now dead and misleading
findings.body: `max_segment_spans` (default 1001) is still accepted by `SpansBuffer.__init__`, but the check that used it was removed from `_load_segment_data` and the Lua script uses a hard-coded 1000. Callers passing this option expect a limit that no longer applies. The 1001 vs 1000 mismatch adds confusion about the real cap.

findings.title: Hard indexing of end_timestamp_precise can crash the whole batch
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError if a span payload lacks the field. `process_batch` has no guard, so one malformed message fails the entire batch and stalls the consumer. The `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` only affects typing, not runtime validation. Consider `.get` with a fallback or explicit per-message handling.

findings.title: Module docstring still describes sets, not sorted sets
findings.body: The module docstring says spans are added to 'the set under set_key' and the glossary describes span-buf:s:* as sets. Storage is now a sorted set scored by end_timestamp_precise, and the score drives the new trimming. The docs are now wrong for anyone debugging Redis state.

findings.title: No tests for the new 1000-span cap, redirect limit, or negative-offset pagination
findings.body: The PR changes the span cap behavior (truncation via zpopmin), the redirect loop limit, and adds a negative-offset paginator path, but adds no tests for any of them. The existing test_basic/test_deep fixtures only use 4-5 spans, so truncation and the score-based eviction order are untested. The paginator changes have no tests at all.

findings.title: Comment claims permissions are enforced by the queryset; it is not
findings.body: The comment says 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' for allowing negative offsets. The queryset only filters by organization_id; the endpoint's permission classes gate access, and nothing in the paginator enforces permissions. The comment misstates the security model and should be removed or corrected.
